reviews.review:
This is a painfully mediocre game. It's a shame because there is a decent base for a game here but everything falls apart with some mindboggling decisions:

- The jetpack sections of the game are by far the best imho, don't really understand why you don't get to keep it for the whole campaign. Every time the protagonist said "Out of fuel" a puppy died.
- Slicing and dicing Orcs for 2/3 of the game gets boring really fast, especially when you are pretty much a one man army. Would prefer more missions like the final assault on the fortress (Chapter 16). It felt epic being in an all Space Marine battle.
- The combat is arkham style and executions are one of the two only ways in the game to get health back. That said, there is no lock on character and executions don't grant you invincibility frames?!

PS. Small rant for the MP aspect of the game:
MP is dead and in order to access the customisation of your space marine (only thing I was interested in), you still have to reach level 4 somehow which roughly translates to 6 solo capture the flag games. Not fun, not fun at all.
Only heretic may dislike this game.
Excellent game! Truly makes you feel like a big man in an even bigger suit of Power Armor. Its even better with friends to fight with/against!
This game is amazing, my only complain is that sometimes the characters are too quiet, the dialogue is just damn good

A resounding meh...

This game is as average as tps shooters come. It's just too standart, too generic and tries to take itself too seriously.

The story follows three ultramarines, who landed on a planet under an orc attack. You might think there is more to it than that, but that sentence is literally the plot. The task is simple, go from point A to B while shooting and hitting orcs. The overal narrative is cliché, predictable and offers no interesting theme or insight. Even for the marines, it felt like just an other Tuesday and the lack of anything interesting in the story and characters is just baffling. There are no character arcs, no underlying themes, no deeper meaning or even twists. Such a big franchise having such a boring game is just awkward.

Even the overall motivation is missing. Why would we want to save this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of a planet? None of the characters are sympathetic and we never see what the planet looked like when it wasn't attacked. All you get is 3 hours worth of rubble.

The graphics and overall level design feels very dated. While the art style was interesting, the areas feel too empty and lifeless. A shorter more focused game might have worked better.

The gameplay is a mixed bag too. The biggest battle is with the camera and overly excessive particle and visual effects and awful slow motion. Half the time, I had no clue what is even happening, due to the camera zooming in and out of geometry or particles obscuring the view. This turns the game into a button smashing exercise, because it's hard to see which character is attacking what and when. Granted the powers do switch up the gameplay, but more clearity would have been nice. Enemy variety is very small unfortunately.

The game is simply too long, and too repetitive, they should have removed like half the runtime and spent that on making better looking environments and more enemies. The whole thing feels like a prolouge mission to a better game, but it doesn't even do that justice, since three hours in and I still didn't know the names of the main characters or any personality traits that would make them unique.

Here are a few themes that a story like this could have touched on:
Crisis of faith, warhammer universe in peacetime, cultural differences between species, theocracy as governing system, abuse of authority, war industry as a sustainable economy etc
